# Third-party source references

The mapper 1–4 adapter in `src/mappers.js` is based on JSNES 2.1.0,
commit `b8a45d088e922b6abcd87c4eb1b7237919e9d3d2`, downloaded from
https://github.com/bfirsh/jsnes on 2026-11-10.

Reference files: `src/mappers/mapper0.js`, `mapper1.js`, `mapper2.js`,
`mapper3.js`, `mapper4.js`, and scanline IRQ hooks in `src/ppu/index.js`.
JSNES is distributed under Apache License 2.0; a copy is in `LICENSE-JSNES.txt`.
Contributor credits are preserved in `references/jsnes/AUTHORS.md` and copied into the release.

The adapter uses page-index tables instead of JSNES's copy-based loaders.
MMC1 mode changes/reset, both single-screen pages, PRG-RAM protection,
MMC3 aligned bank pairs/mode remapping and MMC3B/C IRQ reload semantics were
implemented explicitly, cross-checked with NESdev documentation and test ROMs.
It does not replace the existing jsnes-lite CPU, PPU or audio core.

The jsnes-lite source remains pinned at
`923d45e04483b7655dbdd91773f74de46c38c661` in `upstream/`.

Public diagnostic ROMs used for validation are from
https://github.com/christopherpow/nes-test-roms,
commit `95d8f621ae55cee0d09b91519a8989ae0e64753b`.
They are test inputs, not embedded in the emulator or redistributed with the release.
The original four smoke ROMs under `tests/roms/` are generated by
`tests/make-smoke-roms.mjs` and contain no commercial game data.

V003_003 replaces the v003 oscillator approximation with a compact hybrid APU. Control-register behavior, length/rate tables and sweep conventions were cross-checked with the pinned JSNES APU modules and NESdev reference. It does not bundle the JSNES PCM synthesis engine. Native Web Audio handles tonal synthesis and looping LFSR buffers; the main thread decodes DMC only.

V003_004 uses the existing Base122 packaging adapter (reference commit b62945c2733fa4da8792a1071e40a8b326e8dd1b). The decoder is embedded in the standalone HTML; the reference encoder is build-time only. See LICENSE-BASE122.txt. Keyboard mapping follows project v009.

V003_005 adapts the archive reader from dist/v008-r14-ui/source/src/archive-r14.js, originally imported from the local JSNES r14 player. The existing LZMA core and LZMA2 chunk decoder are retained; the container reader is specialized for one entry and Deflate ZIP / LZMA or LZMA2 7z. The full and short-message versions are saved only as comparison sources/artifacts.

V003_007 replaces the legacy object/prototype LZMA core in the actual runtime with a compact JavaScript LZMA1 implementation. Its probability layout follows the LZMA SDK; the compact state-machine/flat-array approach was informed by Ilya Kurdyukov micro-lzmadec (https://github.com/ilyakurdyukov/micro-lzmadec), commit ebfd2d30d5642551374f999600307d19f7ead269, in particular lzmadec.c and lzmadec.h. No x86 assembly is embedded. The old JS LZMA decoder is retained only as comparison source/artifacts. LZMA2 is not supported by this stage.

V003_008 keeps the V003_007 compact LZMA1 decoder unchanged, removes ZIP, and skips CRC checks in the default runtime. Comparison builds retain JS CRC or extract native CRC32 from a browser-generated gzip trailer.

V003_011: DMC removal comparison against V003_009; upstream checkout unchanged.

V003_012: compact shared-core LZMA2 framing added after checking public-domain 7-Zip and 0BSD XZ decoder specifications; CRC restored. Upstream checkout unchanged.

V003_013: Roadroller scoring adapted in a separate build-only copy; original copyright and LICENSE-ROADROLLER.txt retained. Direct binary six-bit reader used with Base122; upstream checkout unchanged.

V003_014: removed active second-controller implementation and Mapper 30; retained idle second-port bus response. Upstream checkout unchanged.

V003_015: keyboard dictionary replaced by a string array to survive repeated ADVANCED property renaming; old releases remain unchanged.

V003_016: removed CRC calculation, comparisons and stored checksum variables; retained only digest-field skipping for 7z layout. Upstream unchanged.

V003_017: shortened English error codes and filtered unexpected UI errors to six ASCII characters at most; upstream unchanged.
